deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is §6 'Addition' of an early draft of Dedekind's theory of real numbers as cuts (published 1872 as 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen'). The previous page has just finished order properties: every partition of all real numbers into a lower and an upper class is produced by exactly one number; positivity; transitivity.

Main text: first definition of the sum.
- Let alpha, beta be real (rational or irrational) numbers.
- Let a1 range over all rationals with a1 < alpha, and b1 over all rationals with b1 < beta.
- Put C1 = {a1 + b1}.
- Claim (parenthetical): C1 has no greatest element. [My justification, not on the page: the set of rationals < alpha has no maximum, by density.]
- Claim: C1 is a 'first class', i.e. closed downward.
- Proof of downward closure: let c1 = a1 + b1 lie in C1 and c1' < c1, so c1 = c1' + p with rational p > 0. Then c1' = (a1 - p) + b1. Here a1 - p is rational and a1 - p < a1 < alpha, and b1 < beta. Hence c1' lies in C1.
- Let C2 be the set of rationals not in C1. 'Folglich' c2 > c1 always. [Filled in: c2 = c1 is impossible because the classes are disjoint; c2 < c1 would put c2 in C1 by downward closure.]
- So (C1, C2) is a cut. The corresponding real number gamma is defined as alpha + beta.
- Remarks:
  - If alpha and beta are rational, gamma agrees with the old rational sum. Dedekind adds in the margin 'dies besser vorausgeschickt' (better placed earlier). [Filled in: C1 = {q rational : q < alpha + beta}, since any q < alpha + beta can be written as (alpha - d) + (beta - d') with d, d' > 0.]
  - Theorem: alpha + beta = beta + alpha. [Immediate from commutativity of rational addition.]
  - Theorem: alpha + 0 = alpha. [Filled in: every a1 + b1 with b1 < 0 is < a1 < alpha. Conversely, for rational r < alpha choose a rational a1 with r < a1 < alpha and set b1 = r - a1 < 0.]

Right column: alternative formulation ('Oder so'), with A1, B1 now the first classes of the cuts for alpha and beta. It starts with an abandoned sentence, then gives the following.
- Definition: a rational z goes into C1 if there exist a1 in A1 and b1 in B1 with a1 + b1 > z. Otherwise z goes into C2.
- Proof that c1 < c2: if c2 <= c1 < a1 + b1, then c2 < a1 + b1, so c2 would lie in C1, contrary to assumption.
- NB (both classes are nonempty):
  - Pick a1 in A1 and b1 in B1, and rationals a1' < a1, b1' < b1. Then a1' + b1' < a1 + b1, so a1' + b1' lies in C1.
  - Any a2 + b2 (a2 in A2, b2 in B2) lies in C2. [Filled in: a1 < a2 and b1 < b2 for all elements of the first classes, so a1 + b1 < a2 + b2, and no witness exists.]
- Final NB: there is no greatest and no least rational number. This is used for a1' < a1, b1' < b1 and implicitly for the nonemptiness of the classes.

Comparison with print: the 1872 text uses the condition a1 + b1 >= c. The draft's strict '>' makes C1 automatically free of a maximum. Both versions define the same real number.
errors: No real errors. The first version never shows that C2 is nonempty (so that (C1, C2) is a genuine cut); the right-column NB supplies this for the second version.
The parenthetical claim that C1 has no greatest element is stated without proof. It needs the density of rationals below a real number, presumably from earlier sections.
The claims 'gamma agrees with the rational sum when alpha, beta are rational', 'alpha+beta=beta+alpha' and 'alpha+0=alpha' are stated without proof. All are true and easy.

In the first version, A1 means all rationals < alpha. In the second, A1 is the first class of a cut and may contain alpha when alpha is rational. Both give the same gamma, but the switch is not commented on.

results.what: Definition of the sum of two real numbers via the cut generated by sums a1+b1 of lower-class rationals; downward closure and the inequality c1 < c2
results.usually_credited_to: Richard Dedekind (Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen, 1872; ideas from 1858)

results.what: Alternative definition: z in C1 iff there exist a1 in A1, b1 in B1 with a1+b1 > z (strict inequality, versus >= in the printed 1872 text)
results.modern_name: Addition of Dedekind cuts (Minkowski sum of lower sets)

results.what: Commutativity of addition and 0 as additive identity for cuts; consistency with rational addition
results.modern_name: Field axioms for the real numbers (additive part)
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind 1872 (stated); full details in later textbook treatments, e.g. Landau 1930

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of Dedekind's own well-known definition of real addition from 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen'. Drafts in the Nachlass are known (cf. Dugac 1976). The only minor detail is the strict '>' versus the printed '>=', which is of small historical interest.

checkable.asserts: If c1 = a1+b1 and c1 = c1'+p, then c1' = (a1-p)+b1.
For p > 0, a1-p < a1, so a1-p < alpha whenever a1 < alpha.
Example for the rational case: a rational q < alpha+beta is a sum of a rational < alpha and a rational < beta, so the cut sum equals the ordinary sum.
Example for alpha+0=alpha: a rational r < a1 < alpha is a1 + b1 with b1 = r - a1 < 0.

transcription_corrections: 'ein System[?] von rationalen Zahlen C1': the image supports reading 'ein System von rationalen Zahlen C_1' without doubt.

The first, abandoned 'Oder so' line probably reads 'Oder so: Man nehme jede solche (positive?) rationale Zahl c1 auf, für welche'. The transcription's 'Ist[?] Es[?] nehme[?] jede[?] solche[?]' is uncertain; the image suggests '... nehme jede ... rationale Zahl c_1 auf, für welche'.
The struck-out phrase before 'Bezeichnet man mit C2' is not 'Bezeichnet man'. It is a different struck phrase (illegible, possibly 'Folglich ...'), followed by 'Bezeichnet man mit'.
The isolated 'A_1 und B_1' at the top of the right column is a heading/note for the alternative version, where A_1, B_1 denote the first classes of the cuts for alpha, beta.
